text:
ash: Heads-up: security scan flagged a GCR image with a plaintext Vault token in /app/config.json layer. found in a thirdparty-build artifact referenced by staging.

security-bot: Alert: image-scan detected secret-like string matching vault token pattern in image=us.gcr.io/redwood-staging/thirdparty-build:2026-03-23 (scan id: sc-9932).

neha: Which token? CI-runner service token or a long-lived Vault token?

ash: Looks like an env token that a vendor script baked into image at build time. token path: vault://transit/token-prod?role=ci-runner. It decodes like a long-lived token (no explicit TTL).

ryan: Immediate containment: (1) revoke token in Vault, (2) block the image in registry, (3) trigger image garbage-collection and CVE-scan, (4) search for other images with same pattern. I can revoke and block.

infra: On image blocking: we can add a deny tag in registry and update image-promotion webhook. I'll coordinate. For GC we need to coordinate with registry-ops.

ash: Also we need to treat this as potential KMS exposure if that token had unwrap rights. Query: did the token have transit/unwrap or only read secrets?

neha: Checked policy: that token has auth path policies: [kv:readonly, transit:encrypt]. No unwrap. Good. But it's still an auth token skeleton — rotate any creds that were created using that token.

ryan: Revoke done: vault token revoke -self <TOKEN_PLACEHOLDER>. Confirmed revoked at 4945010200.

security-bot: Registry block: added tag block:quarantine to us.gcr.io/redwood-staging/thirdparty-build:2026-03-23 and created ticket REG-4472.

infra: Running image search for similar disclosures: 
```
gcloud container images list-tags us.gcr.io/redwood-staging --format="get(digest, tags)" | xargs -n1 -I{} sh -c 'gcloud container images describe {} --show-package-vuln' || true
# scan layers for token pattern
skopeo inspect --tls-verify=false docker://us.gcr.io/redwood-staging/thirdparty-build:2026-03-23 | jq -r '.Layers[]' | xargs -n1 sh -c 'skopeo inspect --raw docker://{} | strings | grep -E "vault\.[A-Za-z0-9\-_]{20,}" || true'
```

neha: Good. Add RBAC quick-fix: ensure build-runner SA no longer issues long-lived tokens by enforcing token_ttl_max in role binding. I'll push a policy change to Vault: set default-ttl and max-ttl for ci roles.

ash: Also consider KMS key exposure impact: even though token lacked unwrap, check if image build process used a KMS-wrapped secret at build time that might have been unwrapped by build infra. If so, rotate wrapping keys and rewrap artifacts.

ryan: I ran a search of build logs; there was a one-off invocation of gcloud kms decrypt during the build (logs show decrypt with key versions projects/redwood-kms/locations/global/keyRings/build/cryptoKeys/builder-wrap/cryptoKeyVersions/3). We need to rotate that key and re-encrypt any artifacts.

infra: Scheduling KMS rotation requires a rolling rewrap plan. I'll reserve a slot tonight 02:00 UTC to create a new version and rewrap stored artifacts. We must limit to low-traffic windows.

neha: Priority checklist I'm owning:
- [x] Revoke leaked Vault token (ash/ryan confirmed)
- [x] Quarantine image and block in registry (infra confirmed)
- [ ] Search registry for similar tokens (infra in progress)
- [ ] Set Vault role TTL defaults and enforce max-ttl for build roles (PR queued)
- [ ] Rotate KMS wrapping key used by builder and rewrap affected artifacts (scheduled)
- [ ] Trigger CI pipeline to rebuild thirdparty images with fixed buildpack (vendor)
- [ ] Post-incident audit and rotation report

ash: For rewrap, make sure to record rewrap manifest with checksums and push to secure-analytics for verification. We'll ask vendor to re-pull images only after we publish manifests.

ryan: For RBAC belt-and-suspenders: adding a short-lived deny binding on the builder SA with conditions: request.time < now+1h and request.auth.claims.sub != 'ci-service' so we can stop unexpected tokens being minted. Then refine.

infra: Quick command snippets: 
```
# revoke vault token
vault token revoke <token> || true
# create new KMS key version
gcloud kms keys create-key-version --key=builder-wrap --keyring=build --location=global --project=redwood-kms
# rewrap helper
python tools/rewrap_artifacts.py --old-key projects/redwood-kms/.../cryptoKeyVersions/3 --new-key projects/redwood-kms/.../cryptoKeyVersions/4 --manifest out/rewrap-manifest.json
```

neha: Also adding audit logging: forward all vault/audit logs for the build role to SIEM for 90 days. I'll open an observability ticket.

security-bot: Created incident SEC-2026-778 "ci-image token embedded" severity=P2 assigned to eng-security.

ash: Vendor comms: emailed vendor security lead asking them to stop using the compromised image tag and to rebuild with sanitized build steps. vendor asked for our rewrap manifest before pulling new images.

ryan: Infra note: after rewrap and KMS rotation, rotate any ephemeral credentials that the builder might have minted in the last 30d. I'll run a script to list generated tokens and mark for rotation.

neha: Postmortem owner: ash + neha. I'll draft timeline and include recommendations: vault role TTL, pre-publish image scanning, forbid writing /app/config.json at build time, and CI policy enforcement for unallowed patterns.

ash: Closing containment once registry block and revocation done. follow-ups: schedule rotation drill, update build docs for third-party vendors, add pre-publish hook to scan artifacts in CI.

infra: GC requested, registry-ops acked and will prune the quarantined tag after 48h if vendor confirms rebuild.

ryan: search complete: no additional images matched pattern. marking scan as clean at 4945010425.

neha: Thanks team. I'll file the follow-up tickets and assign owners. Good catch. :white_check_mark:
